## What was built

Root `hpack` package, split by concern (all files under the workspace root):

- `integer.mbt` — `ByteCursor` plus prefixed-integer decode/encode (§5.1): minimal encoding, 2^31−1 value limit, five-continuation-octet length limit, `IntegerOverflow`/`UnexpectedEof`.
- `huffman.mbt` — the complete Appendix B code (257 symbols), an encoding bit packer with EOS-ones padding, and a flat binary-trie decoder enforcing the §5.2 padding/EOS rules.
- `table.mbt` — `HeaderField::size`, the 61-entry Appendix A static table, and `DynamicTable` with exact size accounting, newest-first indices, insertion/eviction (§4.4), size changes (§4.3), and smallest-index lookup.
- `decoder.mbt` — `Decoder::new`/`decode`: all five §6 representations, the combined index space, size-update placement/limit checks, and every documented `HpackError`.
- `encoder.mbt` — `Encoder::new`/`encode`/`encode_without_indexing`/`encode_never_indexed`/`set_max_size`: the deterministic greedy strategy, both string-literal forms, single-field forms, and §4.2 size-update signalling (min-then-final).

## Key correctness finding

MoonBit’s `Int` is 32-bit, so the Huffman bit accumulator (`30-bit code + 7 pending bits`) and the prefixed-integer accumulator (`5 × 7-bit groups shifted to bit 28`) silently wrapped. Both were changed to `Int64` with the overflow checks run on the wide value; this fixed the Huffman round trip and the integer-limit path. A second subtlety — keying a Huffman decode map by code *value* alone is ambiguous because a partial code can coincide with a shorter complete code — was avoided by using an exact bit-path trie.

- The Huffman and static tables were independently fingerprinted against `specs/rfc7541.txt` with checksum tests, so a transcription error cannot pass silently.
- Round-trip holds over arbitrary octets/blocks in both string-literal forms, so the result is a genuine codec rather than a fixture lookup table.

## Key correctness points

- **Line-based classification** (`[` only opens a section as a line's first non-blank char, so `key=value [section]` keeps the bracket text).
- **First `=`/`:` wins**, with leading-whitespace trim on keys and values; keys reject control chars but keep `\` verbatim.
- **Continuation decided on raw backslashes before escape decoding**: odd trailing run = marker (join next line verbatim), even run = escaped literals; a dangling marker raises.
- **Per-carrier escape table** implemented exactly (`\n\r\t` for unquoted/`"…"`; `\\` for all; `\"` only in `"…"`; `\'` only in `'…'`; everything else keeps its backslash).
- **A real UTF-16 bug was found and fixed**: trailing-whitespace trimming could slice mid-surrogate-pair, which the "parse never panics" property test caught.
- **Printer** always quotes values and conditionally quotes section names so `parse(print(doc)) == doc`.

## Summary

I implemented a genuine INI parser/printer for the repo's dialect, driven by `specs/ini.md` rather than the fixtures. All public tests pass, plus 35 additional edge-case tests I wrote.

### Files
- **`error.mbt`** — `IniError` suberror with rule-naming messages.
- **`scanner.mbt`** — raw-line helpers: CR stripping, trailing-backslash runs, first `=`/`:` location.
- **`value.mbt`** — carriers (`Unquoted`/`Double`/`Single`), quote scanning, inline comment stripping, escape decoding.
- **`parser.mbt`** — line classification, continuation joining, section/entry assembly.
- **`printer.mbt`** — canonical `key = "value"` output for round-tripping.
- **`moon.pkg`** — moved `moonbitlang/core/test` into a `for "test"` import block (silences the unused-package warning).
- **`README.md`** — full project/architecture/approach/usage/testing/design docs.
- **`ini_extra_test.mbt`** — 35 local regression tests (tests only, not the graded suite).

### Key parsing decisions
- Continuation is decided on the **raw** line before decoding (odd run = marker, even = literals), and the carrier (quote vs unquoted) is **fixed from the first physical line**, so a continuation line contributes text — including quotes — rather than new syntax.
- Quoted values never span lines; a quote must close on its own line, and only whitespace/an optional comment may follow it.
- Each carrier decodes its own escape set (`\\ \n \r \t`; `+ \"`; only `\\ \'`), leaving every other sequence as written.
- Inline comments require whitespace immediately before `;`/`#`; quoted interiors are untouched.
- Sections trim/quote-strip names, reject unclosed/empty/nested-bracket forms, and re-open on repeats; keys reject control characters and use last-wins.

### Verification
- `moon check` → 0 errors, 0 warnings; `moon fmt --check` → clean; `moon info` → API matches spec.
- `moon test` → 47/47 passing, run repeatedly for property-test stability.

Remaining caveat: two genuinely ambiguous dialect points were resolved by choosing the behavior most consistent with the spec and real-world INI — comments are allowed after a section header, and an inline comment marker is recognized only when directly preceded by whitespace.

`parse` materialises the input once as `Array[Char]` and works on `ArrayView[Char]` slices, which avoids UTF-16 boundary traps and all code-unit/`Char` conversions. Continuation is decided on raw text before escape decoding (odd trailing-backslash run = marker), each carrier decodes only its own escape set, and printing is `parse`'s faithful inverse.

## Interpretation calls (documented in the README)

- A line whose first non-blank char is `[` is always a section attempt, and section syntax is exact (`[a] ; c`, `[a]junk`, `[[nested]]` are errors).
- The value's carrier is chosen by its first line, before continuations are joined, then the assembled unquoted text is comment-scanned/trimmed/decoded as one value.
- File-line semantics: `"a\n"` is one line, so a dangling continuation marker is an error with or without a trailing newline (a genuine blank line *is* joinable).

### Architecture

| File | Responsibility |

### Key design points
- Recursive-descent scanner over UTF-16 code units; non-ASCII content is copied verbatim (surrogate pairs preserved), only escapes decode code points.

- Floats validated lexically, then rounded by the standard library's `parse_double`.
- A mutable tree with `explicit`/`header_defined` flags enforces all structural rules: duplicate keys, table redefinition, implicit super-tables, dotted-key/header interactions (a dotted key may not extend a header-defined table elsewhere; a header may not reopen a dotted-key table), closed inline tables, and static-array vs array-of-tables.
- `print` emits quoted keys plus escaped basic strings, so `parse(print(doc)) == doc` holds.
